question_text: Anne places her retirement savings of £400 000 into an annuity fund which returns 4.9% p.a. interest compounded quarterly. She plans to make monthly withdrawals of £3000 from the fund.

subparts.stem: How long will her money last?

mark_breakdown.desc: Set up TVM solver with quarterly compounding $C/Y = 4$ and monthly payments $P/Y = 12$
Determine $N \approx 192.5$ and interpret as 193 months (or 16 years and 1 month)

subparts.solution: $I\% = 4.9$, $PV = -400\,000$, $PMT = 3000$, $FV = 0$, $P/Y = 12$, $C/Y = 4$. $\therefore N \approx 192.5$. Anne's money will last for $193$ months, or $16$ years and $1$ month.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Finding the number of payment periods in an annuity with different compounding and payment frequencies.
step_by_step: Round up to the nearest month for the funds to be fully depleted (193 months).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing $P/Y$ and $C/Y$ when compounding frequency differs from payment frequency.

subparts.stem: How much should she withdraw each month if she wants the money to last for 20 years?
subparts.solution: $N = 20 \times 12 = 240$, $I\% = 4.9$, $PV = -400\,000$, $FV = 0$, $P/Y = 12$, $C/Y = 4$. $\therefore PMT \approx 2613.40$. Anne should withdraw $\$2613.40$ each month.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Computing regular withdrawal amount to deplete a capital over 20 years.
step_by_step: Enter parameters into financial calculator with $C/Y = 4$ and $P/Y = 12$.
